title: Lamb Rogan Josh

extendedIngredients.name: greek yoghurt
extendedIngredients.original: 1/2 cup Greek yoghurt, at room temperature

extendedIngredients.name: fresh ginger
extendedIngredients.original: 15 g fresh ginger, finely grated (a thumb-sized piece)

extendedIngredients.name: fresh coriander
extendedIngredients.original: 1/2 bunch fresh coriander, leaves picked, to serve

steps: Whisk the Greek yoghurt with the mild chilli powder, ground fennel (grind the fennel seeds if whole), ground ginger and 1 teaspoon of salt in a bowl until smooth. Set aside.
Melt the ghee in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat. Add the cinnamon stick, cardamom pods and whole cloves and sizzle for about 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the brown onion and cook, stirring, for 8 minutes until golden. Stir in the garlic and fresh ginger and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the diced lamb and sear, turning the pieces, for about 5 minutes until no longer pink on the outside.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the spiced yoghurt a spoonful at a time so it doesn't split, coating the lamb well.

Return the pot to low heat, add 1 1/2 cups of hot water and a good grind of pepper, then cover and simmer gently for about 1 1/2 hours, stirring now and then, until the lamb is fall-apart tender. Top up with a splash of hot water if it looks dry.
Uncover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes until the gravy is a deep red and thick enough to coat the lamb. Stir in the garam masala and season with salt to taste.

Meanwhile, rinse the basmati rice until the water runs clear, then combine it with 2 1/4 cups of water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to the boil, cover, cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Spoon the curry over the rice and scatter with the fresh coriander leaves to serve.
